title: Joint CT scan
what: Cross-section images of a joint. The bones are seen in 3D and in great detail.
why: For complex fractures, before joint surgery, or when an X-ray did not make everything clear.
duration: usually 5 to 15 minutes in the room; the report the same day or in 1 to 2 days
tell_doctor: If you are or might be pregnant
If the joint has a replacement, a plate, or screws
If CT with contrast is ordered: any allergy to iodine or contrast dye, and kidney disease

prepare.title: Prep
prepare.text: None needed without contrast. You can eat and drink.

prepare.title: Clothing
prepare.text: Take off jewelry and anything metal in the area. Sometimes you are asked to change.

steps: You lie on the table, and the technician helps you get comfortable
The joint is positioned and supported with pillows
The table moves into the ring of the scanner
Keep still for a few seconds
feel: It does not hurt. The scanner hums quietly
The ring is wide, so it does not feel cramped
after: You can go about your day right away
Take the report and images to an orthopedic or trauma doctor

faq.q: CT or MRI of a joint?
faq.a: CT is better for bones and fractures. Ligaments, cartilage, and menisci are seen better on MRI. Your doctor chooses.

faq.q: Can I have a CT with a cast on?
faq.a: Often yes. Ask your doctor. Sometimes the cast is removed.

reminders.text: Joint CT soon. Wear clothes with no metal and bring past images.
